title: Interleaved KV-cache staleness detection and tenant-protect remediation for canary regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Detect and recover from a class of canary regressions caused by interleaved/heterogeneous KV-cache states between model variants and runtime kernel selections. These regressions surface as silent quality drops for a subset of tenants after a canary rollout (often in mixed-hosted/dedicated deployments) where cached KV state is incompatible with the newly served model variant. The goal of this ticket is to add deterministic detection signals, an automated tenant-protect remediation path, and an operator runbook that minimizes blast radius and customer impact across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Alerting rule that detects per-tenant drop in similarity/quality metric (delta > 10% over 15m) correlated with increased token rejection or malformed logits must fire within 5 minutes
A2: Automated remediation that quarantines the affected tenant slice (redirects to last-known-good variant) within 2 minutes of confirmed detection for Hosted and Dedicated environments
A3: Playbook for Private deployments that provides operator CLI steps and idempotent cache-resync script with clear rollback commands
A4: End-to-end QA scenario that reproduces KV-cache mismatch on staging, validates detection, and confirms rollback path restores baseline metrics to within 2% of pre-rollout quality
A5: Post-deployment telemetry dashboard and incident timeline generator linked from Console runtime page
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: Use console alert to identify tenant slices with quality delta > threshold. Confirm regression by running a deterministic prompt set for the tenant and comparing normalized similarity scores to baseline.

2) Fast mitigation (Hosted/Dedicated): Toggle routing policy for affected tenant to 'pin:previous-variant' via routing API (route-change-idempotent). Immediately trigger targeted KV-cache invalidation for the tenant slice (invalidate-prefix: tenant_id:kvcache:*)

3) If quality does not recover within 3 minutes: perform directional rollback of canary slice (reduce canary weight to 0%) and activate fallback model variant cluster. Notify customers in affected slice with templated comms.

4) Private deployments: Notify on-call infra lead, provide operator script (resync_kv.sh) to flush and resync caches from persist layer. If operator cannot run within SLA window, instruct customer to switch traffic to previous image via their orchestrator template (docs included).

5) Post-mitigation: capture full diff of outputs for sample corpus, store the corrupted KV entries for root cause analysis, and escalate to model-onboarding if pattern suggests model-layer incompatibility.

6) Permanent fix: decide between deterministic cache versioning (bump KV namespace on model minor/compat changes) or compatibility shim in runtime. Implement feature flag guarded change and schedule gradual rollout with heavier telemetry.
7) Communication and closure: send internal incident summary to SRE/PM/Support and external brief to impacted customers within 24 hours. Attach reproducible test case and remediation timeline.
rollback_plan: Hosted: automated rollback - pin traffic to stable model variant and invalidate affected KV prefixes; provide temporary traffic-shaping to limit new writes to KV cache during recovery.

Dedicated: orchestration service will stop canary instances and reassign capacity to stable pool; perform cache reconciliation using reconcile-worker job. If reconciliation fails, rollback host image and clear per-tenant caches.

Private: provide operator-run rollback artifact with exact image tag and docker-compose/k8s manifest; include ordered steps to restore DB-backed KV snapshot and restart runtime with 'cache-safe' flag.

Fallback: if rollback not possible immediately, automatically reduce batch size and enable strict deterministic decoding to reduce variance and surface regression symptoms less frequently while remediation proceeds.
telemetry_signals: Token acceptance/rejection rate changes by tenant and route
KV-cache hit/miss ratio and per-prefix error rates
Model variant assignment shifts (routing changes) and steady-state serving kernel selection histogram
Request latency P50/P95/P99 changes for affected tenants
comms_template: We detected an anomaly impacting a subset of requests tied to the recent model rollout. We've redirected your traffic to the previous stable variant and are performing a cache resync. Expected service restoration: within 30 minutes. If you continue to see degraded outputs after that time, please reply with example prompts and request IDs. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident summary.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial triage complete — reproducer identified in staging. Suspect mismatch between kernel-optimizations and cache serialization format introduced in runtime-1.24.
2026-03-11 Luca Martinez: Instrumented additional telemetry (per-tenant hit/miss and serialization errors). Patch merged to staging (PR #4872). Running canary to verify detection firing thresholds.
2026-03-12 Support (Alina Gupta): Drafted customer notification template and queued for review by PM. Identified two enterprise tenants in dedicated clusters that will be notified first.
2026-03-12 QA (Diego Alvarez): Reproducer run shows detection alert fires at 6m; need to tighten threshold to 4m to meet acceptance criteria A1. Updating alert rule and rerunning tests.
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Decided to prioritize detection + automated tenant pin over broad immediate rollback to reduce blast radius.
2026-03-11: Rejected short-term solution of blanket cache flush because it risks invalidating warm caches for high-throughput tenants and may increase latency; moved to targeted prefix invalidation.
2026-03-12: Agreed to add cache-namespace bumping to model-onboarding checklist as medium-term compatibility guarantee.
follow_up_tasks: Add cache-namespace version into model manifest and enforce bump on incompatible changes (owner: Model-Onboarding)
Build dashboard tile that surfaces affected tenant count and time-to-recover for KV-cache regressions (owner: Observability)
Draft runbook tabletop exercise for canary-cached-state regressions and include SRE/Support/PM participants (owner: Reliability)
Post-incident writeup and RCA to be published within 72 hours of incident closure (owner: Incident Lead)
